text:
A year ago we had an idea and an empty whiteboard. Here's where we ended up after twelve months.

We made $180K in revenue. There are four of us now, and I couldn't ask for better people to work with. By month 11 we had 17 paying customers, and they signed up before we had most of the answers.

It wasn't a straight path. We pivoted twice and both pivots failed. Each one taught us something we couldn't have learned any other way, and each "not quite" got us a bit closer to a yes.

A few things I learned this year:

When something fails, treat it as information. Ask what it tells you about the next attempt.

A small team moves fast, but only when everyone is pulling in the same direction.

Your customers will tell you where to go if you listen more than you talk.

To everyone who took a chance on us this year: thank you. I mean it.

On to year two.

What did your first year teach you? I'd like to hear it in the comments.
